prototype.headline: Registering a client and obtaining tokens can often be done within a day, but this may vary.

production.waitTime: Days to weeks if you need to contact support
production.headline: Production use may require contacting Aha! for missing OAuth details and possible plan requirements.

verdict.confidence: medium – OAuth endpoints are confirmed, but many policy and quota details are not documented.
verdict.summary: Aha! exposes OAuth2 metadata on the mcp subdomain, allowing dynamic client registration and standard authorization code flow with PKCE. However, the main site lacks well‑known metadata and the docs do not describe redirect‑URI rules, paid‑plan needs, or review processes, so a prototype is straightforward while production may hit unknown gates.

steps.text: Read the Aha! API documentation which states OAuth2 is the preferred authentication method.
Check the well‑known OAuth metadata; the main domain returns 404, but the mcp subdomain provides metadata.
Identify the registration endpoint from the mcp metadata.

stages.name: Register the application via Dynamic Client Registration

steps.text: POST a registration request to https://mcp.aha.io/oauth/register with required fields (client_name, redirect_uris, etc.).
Include a PKCE S256 code challenge as the server advertises support for it.
Receive client_id and client_secret in the registration response.

stages.name: Configure redirect URI in the Aha! account

steps.text: Add the exact HTTPS redirect URI used in the registration to the app settings (if a UI exists).
If the UI does not accept the URI, contact Aha! support for clarification.

stages.name: Test the OAuth flow via Composio

steps.text: Generate a Connect Link using the client_id and PKCE verifier.
Run the authorization code flow; exchange the code for an access token at the token endpoint.

stages.name: Verify the token works with the API

steps.text: Call a protected API endpoint (e.g., GET /api/v1/features) with the Bearer token and confirm a successful response.

stages.name: Review rate limits and usage quotas

steps.text: Note that API calls are limited to 300 requests per minute per account; no specific OAuth limits are documented.
Ensure any missing requirements (e.g., privacy policy, paid plan) are satisfied; these details are not documented.
If unsure, open a support ticket with Aha! to confirm production‑grade OAuth usage.

requirements: HTTPS redirect URI that exactly matches the one registered
PKCE S256 code challenge for the authorization code flow
A valid Aha! account (any tier that provides API access)

blockers.issue: Redirect‑URI validation rules are undocumented; registration may be rejected if the URI does not meet hidden constraints.
blockers.whenItHits: During stage 3 when adding the redirect URI
blockers.whatToDo: Contact Aha! support to confirm allowed formats or use a known‑good URI.

blockers.issue: Potential paid‑plan requirement for API/OAuth access is not documented.
blockers.whenItHits: When attempting to use the token in production
blockers.whatToDo: Verify your account tier with Aha! sales or support.

blockers.issue: No public app review or verification process is described; unknown if a review is needed for broader user rollout.
blockers.whenItHits: If you plan to allow more than a few internal users
blockers.whatToDo: Ask Aha! support whether an app review is required for public use.

agentCanDo: Generate the Connect Link and handle the PKCE flow
Poll the connection status until ACTIVE
Execute test API calls with the obtained token
Draft a registration payload based on the discovered metadata
youMustDo: Create an Aha! account and ensure it has API access
Submit the dynamic client registration request
Add and verify the redirect URI in the app settings (if a UI exists)
Contact Aha! support for any missing policy or quota information

composioTail: In the Composio dashboard go to Auth Configs, click Create Auth Config, select the toolkit and choose OAuth2.
Copy the redirect URI shown in the Composio dashboard and register it in the provider's app settings.
Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the provider app overview into the Composio auth config, and click Create.
Copy the resulting auth config ID (looks like ac_xxxx). Keep secrets out of source control.
Pass the auth config ID to your session: authConfigs: { [toolkit]: 'ac_xxxx' }. Toolkits not listed keep using Composio managed auth.
